comparison: Perfect alignment on GdnHCl stability claims (C37-C39, C109-C115). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to confounding factors (low fibril concentration) and speculative connection to disease progression. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the differential stability as solid evidence for strain differences without expressing concern about the confounds OpenEval identifies.

Perfect alignment on phosphorylation claims (C76-C86, C156-C159). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the inference about phosphorylation transmission is logical but mechanism remains speculative. Peer reviewers accept these PTM findings as part of comprehensive characterization supporting the main conclusion.

Perfect alignment on main conclusions (C170-C175). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds conclusions appropriately supported by collective evidence. Peer reviewers strongly endorse, calling it 'important work' with 'expansive implications' and suggesting SAA use should be halted until improved methods are developed.

High overlap on PK digestion claims (C40-C51, C116-C119). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to confounding effect of lower fibril concentrations in PD/MSA samples. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting PK resistance data as solid evidence for distinct strains without noting the concentration confound.

High overlap on TEM structural analysis (C58-C75, C143). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive quantitative measurements with statistical support. Peer reviewers accept as part of 'orthogonal biochemical and structural approaches,' noting cryo-EM would strengthen but is outside scope.

Substantial overlap on SAA fibril uniformity claims (C52-C57, C133-C137). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this as a major limitation showing SAA loses intrinsic seed properties. Peer reviewers treat this as the central finding, with both reviewers explicitly endorsing that SAA fibrils don't recapitulate disease-relevant strains.

Partial overlap on seeding kinetics (C29-C31, C34, C36, C87-C88). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on consistent kinetic parameters. Peer R1 also rates as SUPPORTED but includes additional claims (C89-C104, C105, C108) covering confounding factors, PD/MSA comparison, healthy control aggregation, and phosphorylation correlation that OpenEval addresses separately.

Addresses MSA-specific PK digestion pattern (C120-C123). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lower fibril concentration confound. Peer R3 rates as SUPPORTED, grouping MSA findings with broader PK digestion data (C40-C46, C116-C119) as solid evidence for distinct strains.

OpenEval R9 addresses disease duration confounding (C89-C93) as SUPPORTED, finding the PDD/DLB comparison logic sound. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of seeding kinetics and related findings.

OpenEval R10 addresses PD/MSA kinetic indistinguishability (C95-C99) as SUPPORTED with reasonable explanation for CSF study discrepancy. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of seeding kinetics findings.

OpenEval R11 addresses healthy control aggregation (C100-C104) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate documentation of unexpected finding. Peer R1 includes these claims in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of seeding kinetics data.

OpenEval R8 addresses phosphorylation-seeding correlation (C105-C108) as UNCERTAIN due to contradictory literature and lack of mechanistic evidence. Peer R1 includes C105 and C108 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation without specifically addressing the uncertainty about biological role.

OpenEval R13 addresses speculative explanations for SAA fibril properties (C138-C152) as UNCERTAIN, noting plausible but unvalidated hypotheses. Peer R4 groups some of these claims (C138-C146) with SAA uniformity findings rated as SUPPORTED, focusing on the main conclusion rather than mechanistic speculation.

OpenEval R13 includes claims about SAA fibril morphology explanations (C147-C152) rated as UNCERTAIN. Peer R5 includes some overlapping claims in SUPPORTED evaluation of TEM structural findings, not separately addressing the speculative nature of explanations.

Both address prior cryo-EM literature and future work recommendations (C153-C155). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate summary with caveats. Peer R7 explicitly notes cryo-EM would strengthen data but is outside scope, accepting current findings.

OpenEval R12 addresses differential antibody recognition of fibril morphologies (C124-C130) as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about TEM limitations. Peer R7 groups these claims with cryo-EM discussion, accepting findings while acknowledging limitations.

OpenEval R15 addresses prion disease analogy (C160-C164) as UNCERTAIN, noting logical but speculative reasoning requiring validation. Peer R8 rates as SUPPORTED, grouping with broader discussion and explicitly endorsing that SAA material is likely not disease-relevant.

OpenEval R16 addresses literature summary on fibril pathogenicity (C165-C169) as SUPPORTED. Peer R8 groups these claims with prion analogy and methodological limitations discussion, rating as SUPPORTED and strongly endorsing implications for SAA methodology.

OpenEval R18 addresses methodological details (C176-C188) as SUPPORTED, noting standard methods appropriately described. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not separately evaluate methods claims.
